title: Inflection points and transitions in Alzheimer’s disease
authors: Bart De Strooper, Eric Karran
abstract: Inflection points and transitions in Alzheimer’s disease

title: Mechanisms of Transcriptional Regulation by Salicylic Acid Receptors
authors: Yujun Peng, Hainan Tian, Zhenhua Ming, et al.
abstract: Mechanisms of Transcriptional Regulation by Salicylic Acid Receptors

title: Transplanted human brain-tissue takes root in mice without a cortex
authors: Benjamin Thompson, Nick Petrić Howe
abstract: Extensive cellular integration might provide platform for in vivo testing of new therapies — plus, the AI tool that turns papers into ‘virtual corresponding authors’.

title: Development of a random background to understand ligand optimization
authors: Xinyu Xu, Olivier Mailhot, Galen J. Correy, et al.
abstract: An approach to improve efficiency and establish a background expectation for ligand potency optimization is described.

title: Developmental xenocortication using human-derived organoids in mice
authors: Konstantin Kaganovsky, Kevin W. Kelley, Tilo Gschwind, et al.
abstract: Xenocortication with human neurons enables circuit- and behaviour-level analysis of neurodevelopment in mice.

title: Mitochondrial fission factor senses and governs ferroptosis
authors: Songjun Dai, Xiaoyan Dai, Tingting Zhang, et al.
abstract: The mitochondrial–peroxisomal fission adaptor MFF is identified as a selective pro-ferroptotic mediator, and the newly developed MFF–SPARK sensor enables high-content screening of ferroptosis-sensitizing compounds and the discovery of upstream regulators of MFF.

title: Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents
authors: Jiacheng Miao, Joe R. Davis, Yaohui Zhang, et al.
abstract: Paper2Agent converts research papers into interactive artificial intelligence agents by turning manuscripts, code and data into model context protocol-based tool-invoking systems that reproduce original results, answer new scientific queries and collaborate to generate novel insights.

title: Electroluminescent photoresists extending lithographic scaling to OLEDs
authors: Shao-Wei Lo, Sunil B. Shivarudraiah, Zhan-Hong Lin, et al.
abstract: Electroluminescent photoresists synthesized via atom transfer radical polymerization can be directly patterned by ultraviolet and electron-beam lithography, and used to fabricate monolithic, multicolour organic-light-emitting-diode micro-pixel arrays.

title: Continuous-wave laser absorption spectroscopy of the thorium-229 nucleus
authors: I. Morawetz, T. Riebner, L. Toscani De Col, et al.
abstract: Absorption spectroscopy of thorium-229 nuclear excited states in a thorium-doped calcium fluoride crystal demonstrates a path towards a much more efficient way to build a highly stable and robust solid-state optical nuclear clock.

title: Mutational constraints on RSV F and its neutralization by antibodies
authors: Cassandra A. L. Simonich, Teagan E. McMahon, Gavin Juviler, et al.
abstract: How respiratory syncytial virus mutations affect antibody neutralization is defined, and a biophysical model of the mechanism is provided, to show how Fab potency and epitope specificity combine to determine the effects of viral mutations on antibody neutralization.

title: Evolution and heterogeneity of lethal metastatic bladder cancer subtypes
authors: Pushpa Itagi, Samantha L. Schuster, Sonali Arora, et al.
abstract: A rapid autopsy programme provides valuable resources to enable detailed molecular and genetic analyses of the temporal evolution of aggressive histological subtypes and therapy resistance in metastatic bladder cancer.

title: Topographic structure and function of locus coeruleus noradrenaline neurons
authors: Zhixiao Su, Polina Kosillo, Kanghoon Jung, et al.
abstract: Dorsal and ventral noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus form topographic subpopulations whose projection patterns and activity encode choice switching, reward-prediction errors and disregard of reward-predictive cues, supporting flexible learning behaviour.

title: Overmassive black holes and little red dots naturally form in simulations
authors: Sunmyon Chon, Shingo Hirano, Tomoaki Ishiyama, et al.
abstract: Observations from the JWST reveal an unexpectedly abundant population of little red dots and overmassive black holes in the early Universe, which are confirmed by their formation in fully cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations.

title: A retinoic acid autoregulatory loop governing prefrontal–motor arealization
authors: Lin Yang, Mikihito Shibata, Saejeong Park, et al.
abstract: MEIS2, encoding a transcription factor linked to intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, is a key hub of a retinoic-acid-associated gene regulatory network.

title: Road transport of trapped antiprotons
authors: M. Leonhardt, J. Morgner, F. Abbass, et al.
abstract: Researchers demonstrate successful road transport of trapped antiprotons, establishing a practical method for moving antimatter to quieter laboratories and substantially improving future tests of matter–antimatter symmetry.

title: Transcriptional activation of plant immunity by salicylic acid
authors: Songwen Zhang, Madeline Gish, Huan Li, et al.
abstract: A mechanistic basis for how the hormone salicylic acid promotes transcriptional activation during plant immune responses is described.

title: Rapid patient-specific neural networks for X-ray to volume registration
authors: Vivek Gopalakrishnan, David-Dimitris Chlorogiannis, Andrew Abumoussa, et al.
abstract: xvr makes pan-anatomical 2D/3D rigid registration accessible to broad clinical and research communities.

title: Heterogeneous photonic integration of single-crystalline nanomembranes
authors: Yuan Meng, Wenbo Mao, Zhihao Xu, et al.
abstract: A framework consisting of advanced epitaxy and layer lift-off techniques uses heterogeneous photonic integration of single-crystalline nanomembranes to infuse desired functionalities into silicon and silicon nitride photonics, demonstrating ultraefficient electro-optical and magneto-optical modulation.

title: Molecular-level observation of the self-assembly of a virus-like particle
authors: Roi Asor, Dan Loewenthal, Diana Melnyk, et al.
abstract: Using mass photometry combined with a single-molecule trapping method allows real-time monitoring of the assembly of individual virus-like particles with molecular resolution, enabling observation and quantification of their self-assembly pathways and dynamics.

title: Targeted genomic integration and rearrangement using prime assembly
authors: Sébastien Levesque, Nozomu Kawashima, Gue-Ho Hwang, et al.
abstract: Prime assembly enables RNA-guided integration of medium-to-large DNA sequences in human cells without requiring double-strand breaks or cell cycle progression, and supports exon recoding, transgene insertion and megabase-scale rearrangements.

title: Sex without crossovers mimics clonal reproduction in Rhynchospora tenuis
authors: Meng Zhang, Marco Castellani, Stefan Steckenborn, et al.
abstract: Rhynchospora tenuis undergoes obligate, genome-wide achiasmy in both male and female meiosis.

title: Scalable near-real-time Bayesian phylogenetics for outbreaks with Delphy
authors: Patrick Varilly, Mark Schifferli, Katherine Yang, et al.
abstract: Delphy makes near-real-time and scalable Bayesian phylogenetics possible for growing viral outbreaks, enabling public health bodies anywhere to analyse and react to their own data with state-of-the-art accuracy and minimal friction.

title: Author Correction: Obesity rise plateaus in developed nations and accelerates in developing nations
authors: Bin Zhou, Nowell H. Phelps, Agnese Galeazzi, et al.
abstract: Author Correction: Obesity rise plateaus in developed nations and accelerates in developing nations

title: Electrically controllable superconducting memory effect in UTe 2
authors: Zheyu Wu, Hanyi Chen, Mengmeng Long, et al.
abstract: Observations of a memory effect in the p-wave superconductor candidate UTe2, which can be controlled by varying the strength and duration of the electrically applied stimuli, are described.

title: Cohesin reshapes replication fork contacts to aid fork slowing and reversal
authors: Daniel González-Acosta, Daniel Giménez-Llorente, Melani Rodrigues, et al.
abstract: Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion limits sister-fork coupling and tethers nearby replication forks under replication stress, promoting fork reversal and slowing fork progression to safeguard genome stability.

title: Assessing biological degradation of non-hydrolysable synthetic polymers
authors: Anton A. Stepnov, Allison Werner, Soo-Jin Yeom, et al.
abstract: The evidence for biological degradation of non-hydrolysable synthetic polymers is critically evaluated to propose best-practice principles for experimental design that should promote reproducibility and impact across this field.

title: Identification of broadly tumour-reactive γδ TCRs from multiple myeloma
authors: Michael St. Paul, Liam D. Hendrikse, Fan Ying, et al.
abstract: A machine-learning algorithm, PreGame, is developed to identify tumour-reactive γδ T cells from single-cell CITE sequencing data, and expansion of this cell population can be used as a biomarker of therapeutic response.

title: Predictors and prevalence of support for white nationalism in the United States
authors: Patrick J. Egan, James Bisbee, Joshua A. Tucker
abstract: Explicit support for white nationalism is uncommon overall, but higher among young white men, disadvantaged and politically disaffected white people, conservatives, Republicans, and those with primarily online friendships.

title: A thermodynamically favoured molecular computer
authors: Tristan Stérin, Abeer Eshra, Constantine Glen Evans, et al.
abstract: Scaffolded DNA Computer performs diverse computations while thermodynamically relaxing towards equilibrium, demonstrating simplicity, reusability, speed, robustness and scalability of the approach by running 10 programs, including parity, multiplication and 25-bit addition.

title: Marine bacteria cooperate to break down complex algal carbohydrates
abstract: Marine algae produce sulfated carbohydrates called fucoidans that are chemically too complex for any bacteria to digest alone. Instead, marine bacteria split the task between them in a modular fashion: some strains degrade the molecular backbone, whereas others remove the side branches.

title: Antimatter: coming soon to a lab near you?
authors: Nancy Paul, Davide Gamba
abstract: Antiprotons have been transported by road at CERN. This advance might one day enable laboratories outside the site to use antimatter in their experiments.

title: Molecular computation that rolls energetically downhill
abstract: A DNA-based computer that operates by relaxing to thermodynamic equilibrium has been demonstrated on ten molecular programs, which completed computations in as little as one minute. Some programs were rerun using distinct inputs up to 25 times and others were scaled up to 100-bit computations — although this slowed them down substantially.

title: Turning scientific research papers into interactive AI agents
abstract: Scientific knowledge is mostly stored in static papers. An automated framework called Paper2Agent can now transform each paper into an active artificial intelligence agent — a virtual corresponding author that answers questions, applies the paper’s methods to new data, and collaborates with other paper agents. This makes research easier to reproduce, reuse and extend.

title: Is it safe to use consumer wearable devices for research?
authors: Virginia Gewin
abstract: Wearable technology is a boon for studying health behaviours, but it comes with some thorny ethical concerns, says researcher Wuyoh Sui.

title: Nearly one in seven young, male white voters in the US support white nationalism
authors: Jennifer Chudy
abstract: Three national surveys reveal how factors such as gender, age, political alignment and income are correlated with support for white nationalism in the United States.

title: Map of brain ‘microproteins’ could offer new clues to Alzheimer’s disease
authors: Miryam Naddaf
abstract: Researchers detect more than 1,000 overlooked microproteins in human brain tissue, including some that are altered in Alzheimer’s disease.

title: AI companies must work with the research community to protect attribution
abstract: An era-defining mathematics claim raises questions over how AI tools credit earlier work.

title: Will wearable technologies transform clinical trials?
authors: Nic Fleming
abstract: Digital wearables are increasingly being used in a research setting, but their scientific rigour and impact are subjects of debate.

title: Human brain cells transplanted into mice in ‘most extensive’ integration ever
authors: Max Kozlov
abstract: Lab-grown organoids wire into mice missing a key part of their brain, offering a new way to test drugs for developmental conditions.

title: These bizarre, much-coveted microbes are revealing the origins of complex life
authors: Elizabeth Quill
abstract: Researchers are racing to culture a menagerie of exotic organisms and finding lots of surprises along the way.

title: Tumour cells shape their environment to protect them from the immune system
abstract: A subset of pancreatic cancer cells express the genes SERPINE1 or SERPINB2, which form a molecular mesh around them. This sticky matrix helps to retain immunosuppressive cells and exclude the immune cells that kill cancer cells. Disrupting this process in mice improves immune control of pancreatic tumours and sensitizes them to immunotherapy.

title: AI tool turns any paper into an ‘agent’ that can collaborate and answer complex queries
authors: Kaia Glickman
abstract: The Paper2Agent system makes it easier for researchers to reproduce papers and understand work in unfamiliar fields, authors say.

title: I who have never known trees
authors: Hannah Cocks
abstract: Lost connections.

title: Virus-like particles observed assembling in real time
authors: Charlotte Uetrecht
abstract: Scientists have long dreamt of being able to track and analyse each step in the assembly of a virus’s protein shell. An ingenious experiment shows how this can be done.

title: Three-dimensional chromatin architecture is rapidly restored after DNA replication
authors: Tyler K. Fenstermaker, Svetlana Petruk, Alexander Mazo
abstract: Here, the authors show that factors involved in DNA looping bind DNA immediately after replisome passage and that loops are reformed within 10 min of DNA replication.

title: Learning stochasticity via a nonparametric approach to state-dependent noise estimation
authors: G. Pillonetto, A. Giaretta, M. Bisiacco
abstract: Trine is a nonparametric kernel-based framework for inferring state-dependent noise from time-series data. Using a three-stage regression approach, it uncovers hidden stochastic dynamics without requiring predefined functional forms.

title: Leveraging design for collective phototaxis in morphological swarm robotics
authors: Jeremy Fersula, Nicolas Bredeche, Olivier Dauchot
abstract: Careful design of robots morphology leverage interactions for collective behaviors from little computation as demonstrated through experimental realizations and faithful simulations of a swarm of robots performing phototaxis.

title: Sparse X-ray spectro-tomography for high-sensitivity three-dimensional chemical imaging at the nanoscale
authors: Hanfei Yan, Ajith Pattammattel, Aaron Michelson, et al.
abstract: The study introduces a sparse spectro‑tomography method that cuts data needs in scanning mode by about two orders of magnitude, enabling high-sensitivity, low‑dose 3D chemical imaging. It uncovers surface Co reduction and Mn loss in battery particles, revealing key degradation pathways.

title: Dynamical signatures of conventional and asymptotic quantum many-body scars on a trapped ion simulator
authors: Leonard Logarić, John Goold, Shane Dooley
abstract: Using a trapped-ion quantum computer, the authors report experimental evidence of ‘asymptotic quantum scars’ - special states that resist thermal equilibrium more as system size grows.

title: Structural and functional insights into a Zn 2+ -transporting P-type ATPase
authors: Pin Lyu, Elena Longhin, Fatemeh Sabzian-Molaei, et al.
abstract: Zinc is essential for cellular metal homeostasis, but the molecular mechanisms of zinc-transporters remain poorly understood. Here, the authors reveal the structure and regulatory mechanism of a zinc-transporting P-type ATPase, providing insights into zinc uptake and autoregulation.

title: Practical synthesis of 3-Oxa/Aza-bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes from 3-Oxa/Aza[3.1.1]propellanes
authors: Qin Jiang, Jianyang Dong, Fang Lei, et al.
abstract: While bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanes (BCPs) and bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes (BCHeps) serve as established 3D bioisosteres for para- and meta-substituted benzenes, accessible via ring-opening of their corresponding propellanes, the integration of heteroatoms into these propellane scaffolds has remained elusive. Herein, the authors report the practical synthesis of 3-oxa/aza[3.1.1]propellanes, two heteroatom-con

title: Epithelial-mesenchymal Wnt crosstalk directs planar cell polarity in the developing cochlea
authors: Ippei Kishimoto, Abel P. David, Kevin P. Rose, et al.
abstract: Patterning of cochlear hair cells is governed by planar cell polarity. Here, the authors show that multiple Wnt proteins from epithelial and mesenchymal compartments control cochlear elongation, hair cell patterning and core planar cell polarity proteins.

title: Engaging figures
authors: Helena Klara Jambor, Fateme Rajabiyazdi, Verena Prantl, et al.
abstract: Some visualizations resonate while others are forgotten. Why that is can be understood with the principles of creating ‘proximity’.

title: When a laser beam hits an electron beam
authors: Vivien Marx
abstract: Prototypes of specially engineered transmission electron microscopes deliver images with greatly improved contrast to cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) projects.
